requirements.requirement: Inventory application is served on TCP port 8181 on node1
requirements.summary: httpd was installed and configured with a VirtualHost listening on 8181, serving inventory content. curl returned HTTP 200 with the expected inventory HTML both immediately after configuration (cmd-ec06d861234e4b87) and again after a full node restart (cmd-fed592b81bb54f9d). The after-executor lifecycle snapshot independently confirms httpd listening on *:8181 (global:after_executor:node1:listening-sockets).

requirements.requirement: SELinux (mandatory access control) remains in enforcing mode throughout
requirements.summary: Baseline showed SELinux Enforcing (cmd-31d58989242a43ed). Enforcing mode was preserved during and after configuring the port context and httpd (cmd-ec06d861234e4b87), confirmed again in the pre-restart baseline (cmd-41e4ed1ba10d4705), and confirmed post-restart (cmd-fed592b81bb54f9d). Port access was enabled via semanage port policy (http_port_t) rather than disabling enforcement, and no AVC denials were recorded at any checkpoint.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and demonstrates healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and full recovery for node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id, SELinux enforcing, httpd active, HTTP 200 (cmd-41e4ed1ba10d4705). Reboot was acknowledged via systemd-run (cmd-de746a51c8bd481b), confirmed by transient connection failures during the outage (cmd-15542e40297443d9, cmd-7981c693d9f340be). A new boot_id was observed post-restart (cmd-56d3aa5dff3e4b91), matching the fixed global boot-identity snapshots (06339ff3... before, ab498815... after). Post-restart recovery of SELinux enforcing, httpd, port 8181 listener, SELinux port policy, firewall rule, and inventory content was directly verified (cmd-fed592b81bb54f9d).

overall_summary: The executor deployed the inventory application behind httpd on TCP port 8181 on node1 while keeping SELinux enforcing throughout, using the correct semanage port-context approach rather than weakening enforcement. Both material task outcomes are directly and repeatedly verified (pre- and post-restart). The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also executed cleanly and completely, showing a healthy baseline, a genuine restart (boot_id change), and full post-restart recovery of service, SELinux, firewall, and content state.
limitations: Two small temp files (/tmp/curl_out.html, /tmp/dnf_install.log) generated during configuration were left on node1; not cleaned up, though low-risk and not functionally significant.
AVC denial checks relied on ausearch scoped to 'recent'/'boot' windows rather than a full audit log review, so denials outside those windows (if any) would not be captured.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task: package install, docroot creation, httpd VirtualHost config, restorecon, semanage port policy, firewalld rule, service enable/start, and the required restart protocol — no unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found. Minor residue: /tmp/curl_out.html and /tmp/dnf_install.log created by cmd-ec06d861234e4b87 were left on the system (visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot) rather than cleaned up; this is a bounded, low-risk leftover rather than a functional problem.
